title: Paeoniflorin Ameliorates Alcohol-Induced Depression via Modulating the Gut-Brain Axis and Inhibiting the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 Inflammasome Pathway in Mice.
authors: Yu, Jingwei; Zhang, Ruijing; Quan, Yingshi; Sun, Dingchun; Huang, Chao; Xu, Jiaqi; Li, Xiangdan; Liu, Lan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究芍药苷通过肠-脑轴和NF-κB/NLRP3通路改善酒精诱导抑郁，核心为神经炎症与肠道菌群，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Paeoniflorin (PF), the primary bioactive component of Paeonia plants, exhibits neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory activities. However, its potential role in alcohol-induced depression (AID) through the microbiota-metabolite-brain axis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the antidepressant effect of PF and its underlying gut-brain communication mechanisms. A mouse model of chronic alcohol exposure was established and treated with PF. Behavioral tests (SPT, FST, TST, OFT) and histopathological examinations were conducted. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict targets, followed by experimental validation of microglial activation and the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 pathway. Multi-omics approaches including 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics were applied to analyze gut microbiota and fecal metabolites. PF significantly alleviated depressive-like behaviors, hippocampal damage, and oxidative stress, while restoring monoamine neurotransmitter levels. It suppressed microglial activation and the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 inflammasome cascade. Furthermore, PF reshaped gut microbiota composition (reducing Rikenellaceae and Prevotellaceae) and modulated metabolite profiles and upregulated the neuroprotective metabolite niacin, along with other identified metabolites. These findings demonstrate that PF alleviates Alcohol-Induced Depression (AID) by remodeling the microbiota-metabolite-brain axis and inhibiting neuroinflammation. The study highlights PF's therapeutic potential for alcohol-related mood disorders and underscores the gut-brain axis as a critical target for antidepressant therapy.
abstract_zh: 芍药苷（PF）是芍药属植物的主要生物活性成分，具有神经保护和抗炎活性。然而，其通过微生物-代谢物-脑轴在酒精诱导抑郁（AID）中的潜在作用仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨PF的抗抑郁效果及其潜在的肠-脑通讯机制。建立慢性酒精暴露小鼠模型并给予PF处理。进行行为学测试（SPT、FST、TST、OFT）和组织病理学检查。采用网络药理学和分子对接预测靶点，随后通过实验验证小胶质细胞活化和NF-kappaB/NLRP3通路。应用多组学方法，包括16S rRNA测序和非靶向代谢组学，分析肠道微生物群和粪便代谢物。PF显著缓解了抑郁样行为、海马损伤和氧化应激，同时恢复单胺类神经递质水平。它抑制了小胶质细胞活化和NF-kappaB/NLRP3炎症小体级联反应。此外，PF重塑了肠道微生物群组成（减少Rikenellaceae和Prevotellaceae），调节代谢物谱，并上调神经保护性代谢物烟酸及其他已鉴定的代谢物。这些发现表明，PF通过重塑微生物-代谢物-脑轴和抑制神经炎症来缓解酒精诱导抑郁（AID）。该研究强调了PF在酒精相关情绪障碍中的治疗潜力，并突出了肠-脑轴作为抗抑郁治疗的关键靶点。
